title: When Consumer Financial Protection Spills Over: Student Loan Borrowing Under the CARD Act
authors: Alexander L. Brown; Daniel Grodzicki; Paolina C. Medina
eligible_reason: Main-text design has a single policy date: Post = 1[Semester >= 2011-3] (01_cleanup.do line 302) and Treat = sophomore or junior standing (a within-student time-varying status, line 305), estimated on student-semester records with Semester x median-income FE, class-standing dummies and demographic controls, clustered by student (03_borrowing_regs.do lines 42-62); event study interacts Treat with semester dummies. No unit FE and no unit-specific adoption dates in the main text. An appendix Callaway-Sant'Anna check (08_csdid.R) defines cohorts by first-enrollment year (semtreat = 9/11/13 for 2010/2011/2012 entrants) with not-yet-treated controls, but it is an appendix robustness and its design differs from the main text.
design_notes: Administrative financial-aid records of a large US public university (confidential); outcomes YL/TL/YFafsa (borrowing indicators and amounts). Figures 1-2: reghdfe y DS*_Treat Sophomore Junior Senior Male Minority InStateStudent ufreshfafsa, abs(Semester#MedInc) vce(cluster StudentID). Figure 3 academic outcomes with FirstEnrollYear and MedInc FE. Survey analysis Tables 2-5; welfare Table 6. Replication data are cell-level aggregates (cells with >100 students, ~60% of sample).
estimators_reported: two-group DiD / event study with controls (reghdfe, Semester x MedInc FE)
Callaway-Sant'Anna att_gt (appendix, cohorts by enrollment year)
data_files: data/aggregate_borrowing.dta|csv, data/aggregate_outcomes.dta|csv (cell means, >100 students per cell)
output/master_log_raw_data.log (full regression output on confidential micro data)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Main text: one policy date. Appendix csdid: 3 enrollment-year cohorts (2010, 2011, 2012).
data_files_note: Raw student records under NDA; only aggregates shipped.
software_notes: Stata 17 (reghdfe, coefplot, estout) + R (did) for appendix
